validity.recommendation: no structural change; add the refs staged here to Status/Fuel/Start/Length/Location/Operator/Owner
validity.researcher_notes: Existence, classification, ownership, length, start year and route are all independently confirmed. Empire Pipeline, Inc. is a real FERC-regulated (NGA-jurisdictional) interstate gas transmission subsidiary of National Fuel Gas Company, headquartered Williamsville, NY -- confirmed by (1) a 2002 SEC 8-K exhibit (National Fuel's press release announcing its acquisition of the then-'Empire State Pipeline' from Duke Energy: 'Constructed in 1992 and in service since 1993 ... a 24-inch diameter natural gas transmission pipeline that originates at the United States/Canada border at the Chippawa Channel of the Niagara River ... extends easterly 157 miles from Buffalo, N.Y., to near Syracuse, N.Y.'), (2) an independent Oil & Gas Journal article on the same transaction restating the identical specs, (3) a FERC Federal Register notice (Docket CP10-493-000, Sept. 2010) for the 'Tioga County Extension Project' -- 'approximately 16 miles of 24-inch diameter natural gas pipeline extending [Empire's] existing system from its interconnection with ... Millennium Pipeline ... in Corning, New York to new producer interconnections in Tioga County, Pennsylvania' -- confirming the PA terminus and a later build phase, (4) a PHMSA special-permit FEA/FONSI (Docket PHMSA-2017-0158) describing the 'Empire Connector Pipeline (ECP)' as a real, operating 76.6-mile, 24-inch OD, X-70 steel line under an active MAOP special permit, and (5) an EIA weekly natural gas report (week of Oct. 9, 2013) independently naming 'the Empire Pipeline (in Grand Island, NY)' as one of the Niagara Falls-area US/Canada border crossings amid the Marcellus-driven flow reversal at Niagara -- fully independent of National Fuel. Operator's own current page (nationalfuel.com) states the present-day aggregate system is 'approximately 269-mile,' matching the sheet's LengthKnown=269.00 exactly, and gives the build-out arithmetic that explains it: 157 mi (1993, Chippawa->Oswego County NY) + 77 mi Empire Connector (2008, to Corning NY) + 15 mi Tioga County Extension (Nov. 2011, to Tioga County PA) + 17 mi Tuscarora Lateral (late 2015, closing the gap in Steuben County NY) = a 269-mile system whose southern end is genuinely in Tioga County, Pennsylvania -- so EndPrefecture/District='Tioga' and EndState/Province='Pennsylvania' are correct, as is StartLocation='Chippawa'/StartState/Province='Ontario' (the Canadian-side town directly across the Niagara River from the Grand Island, NY border crossing the operator's page cites). Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, StartYear1=1993, Owner1='Empire Pipeline' 100% are all consistent with every source read. CAVEAT: the sheet's 'Main Line' row is an aggregate of four separate build phases spanning 1993-2015 (not one project), so a single system-wide Pressure or SegmentCost figure does not exist and I have not forced one (see fills[] -- both left UNRESOLVED with the reason). I read the gem.wiki Empire_Pipeline page itself (not cited) and it correctly separates 'Main Line' from the 2020 'Empire North Expansion Project' (a different PID, P2531) and two CANCELLED 'Northern Access 2016' expansion projects -- those two cancelled projects are why 11 of this row's 15 harvested wiki citations are Northern-Access-specific news (Reuters, Utility Dive, NGI, Buffalo News, wkbw.com, a lockportjournal.com piece, a bit.ly link) that do not bear on the Main Line row at all; I opened/resolved all 15 of P0288's harvested citations (the bit.ly one resolves to a National Fuel PDF landing page, now presumably stale) and none were usable as Main-Line refs beyond confirming the Northern Access cancellation is real (consistent with Status not being asked to change on this row). Opened well beyond the harvested pool: SEC EDGAR, Oil & Gas Journal, 2 Federal Register notices, a PHMSA docket PDF, an EIA weekly archive page, and Empire's own FERC Gas Tariff PDF (8.3 MB, searched but did not locate a single clean 'system design capacity' line -- see the Capacity concern below).

validity.recommendation: re-research current system Capacity before adding a ref to the Capacity cell; do not cite the RBN Energy 'Empire North Expansion' article for the Main Line's capacity
validity.researcher_notes: The current Capacity value (300.00 MMcf/d) is unsupported as sourced and materially disputed by an independent record. Reading the gem.wiki page itself (not cited): the 'Main Line' section's ONLY footnote for 'Capacity: 300 million cubic feet per day [1]' is citation [1], which is 'Empire North Expansion, RBN Energy' -- an article about the DIFFERENT, later (2020) Empire North Expansion Project (GEM's own separate row, P2531), not about the Main Line. P2531's own recorded capacity is ALSO 300.00 MMcf/d, which is exactly the coincidence the sweep brief flagged as suspicious. Independently, a 2002 SEC 8-K exhibit (National Fuel's press release on acquiring the original 157-mile pipeline from Duke Energy) and a same-vintage Oil & Gas Journal article both state the original mainline segment's 'design capacity' as 525 million cubic feet per day (525 MMcf/d) -- nearly double the value currently on the sheet. I could not confirm whether 525 MMcf/d (a 1992-93, 157-mile-segment figure, before the 2008/2011/2015/2020 expansions and added compression) is still the right figure for TODAY's full 269-mile aggregate system, so I am not proposing a replacement number -- only flagging that the currently-cited chain of support is broken and the true value is unresolved between roughly 300 and 525+ MMcf/d. I searched Empire's own current FERC Gas Tariff (informationalpostings.natfuel.com/empire/docs/empiretariff.pdf, 8.3 MB) for a clean system capacity figure and could not locate one in a full-text search (it lists per-shipper contract MDQs, e.g. 150,000 and 200,000 Dth/d, but no aggregate system total); recommend Update pull a recent FERC Form 2/2-A or an NFG investor-relations pipeline capacity table, or search the tariff PDF's rate-schedule tables directly (not full-text-searchable everywhere), to pin the current number.

verifications.note: National Fuel's 2002 press release (SEC 8-K exhibit): 'Empire is a 24-inch diameter natural gas transmission pipeline' (the original 157-mile segment).
PHMSA special-permit docket: 'the Empire Connector Pipeline (ECP)... 76.6 mile, 24-inch outside diameter... natural gas steel pipeline.'
FERC Federal Register notice, Docket CP10-493-000: Tioga County Extension = 'approximately 16 miles of 24-inch diameter natural gas pipeline.'

fills.researcher_notes: 24-inch is independently confirmed across three separate build phases covering roughly 250 of the row's 269 miles (157-mi original 1992/93 segment per SEC 8-K + Oil & Gas Journal; 76.6-mi Empire Connector per PHMSA; 16-mi Tioga County Extension per FERC). No source anywhere states a different diameter for any portion of this system, so 24 in is staged as the row's single Diameter value; the ~17-mi 2015 Tuscarora Lateral's own diameter was not separately confirmed but is a minor share of total mileage.

verifications.note: 'Constructed in 1992 and in service since 1993, Empire delivers natural gas supplies...'
'The system, which was constructed in 1992 and put into service a year later...' -- independent trade-press confirmation of the same fact, not a reprint of the NFG release.

fills.researcher_notes: Matches and corroborates the row's existing StartYear1=1993 (in-service the year after construction). This applies to the original 157-mile phase only, which is what StartYear1 also represents (the row's earliest phase) -- ConstructionMonth not stated by either source, left blank rather than guessed.

Searched FERC's Federal Register archive, SEC EDGAR, Oil & Gas Journal and general web for an original certificate application/proposal date for the pre-1992 project (would be a ~1990-1991 FERC Natural Gas Act filing); nothing pre-1993 surfaced beyond 'constructed in 1992' (which is staged as ConstructionYear). FERC eLibrary's full-text index does not reliably cover filings this old. Left UNRESOLVED rather than inferring a year from the construction date.

The only MAOP figures found are segment/class-location-specific and only for the Empire Connector portion: PHMSA's 2017-0158 special-permit docket states the ECP's MAOP was increased from 1,290 psig to 1,440 psig on the special-permit (Class 1 location) segment only, with other class locations at different values by design factor. No single system-wide MAOP or operating-pressure figure was found (the FERC tariff PDF searched for the Diameter/Capacity fills also does not state one). Rather than force a value that would misrepresent a multi-class-location system as one pressure, left UNRESOLVED.

verifications.note: Operator's own page: Empire's expansions let it 'offer abundant, reliable and economical supplies of regionally produced natural gas, including less expensive Marcellus gas supplies.'

fills.researcher_notes: Value matches the existing controlled-vocabulary form 'Marcellus/Utica natural gas' used elsewhere in the GGIT sheet. Only source found is National Fuel itself (the operator), so tier=medium and independent=false. Searched for a second, non-operator source: an EIA weekly natural gas report (Oct. 2013) discusses Marcellus-driven gas-flow reversal at the Niagara Falls-area border crossings, naming Empire Pipeline as one of those crossings, but does not itself state that Empire specifically carries Marcellus/Utica gas (it is about the corridor generally, TGP's 300 Line, not Empire's own receipt points) -- so it was not used as the second independent source. No other second source located within the time available; a dedicated NFG 10-K search (SEC EDGAR) would likely state Empire's own receipt-point sourcing explicitly and is the next place to look.

No single project cost applies to this aggregate, multi-phase row. Two cost figures were found but neither fits: (1) the 2010 Tioga County Extension sub-project alone was estimated at ~$45.9 million per the FERC Federal Register notice (Docket CP10-493-000) -- that is one 16-mile phase's cost, not the whole Main Line's; (2) National Fuel's 2002 acquisition of the original 157-mile pipeline from Duke Energy was $240 million (incl. $60 million assumed debt) per the SEC 8-K and Oil & Gas Journal -- that is an acquisition/purchase price, not a construction capital cost, and is the wrong kind of figure for SegmentCost. Left UNRESOLVED rather than staging either mismatched number.

verifications.note: 'Empire Pipeline, Inc. (Empire) is headquartered in Williamsville, NY, and is one of two FERC-regulated subsidiaries of National Fuel Gas Company...'
'Empire Pipeline, Inc. (Empire) is operator of the Empire Connector Pipeline (ECP).' -- independent federal docket confirming the same operator name.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (operator's own site; PHMSA federal special-permit docket) agree Empire Pipeline, Inc. is the operator, consistent with the existing Owner1='Empire Pipeline' 100%.

cross_row_leads.facts: Operator's own page: 'In 2020 Empire placed the Empire North Project into service, which saw the construction of two new compressor stations, the Jackson Compressor Station and the Farmington Compressor Station. The project created firm incremental capacity...' -- i.e., National Fuel itself describes the 2020 Empire North Project as COMPRESSION ONLY, no new pipeline mileage. This directly conflicts with gem.wiki's (and apparently P2531's) recorded Length=40.2 km/25 mi and Diameter=26-in for the 'Empire North Expansion Project,' which read as if it were a discrete new pipe segment. Worth a spec/classification check on P2531: was 25 mi of NEW pipe actually built alongside the two compressor stations, or is the 40.2 km figure a mismeasure/misattribution? FERC's docket for this project is No. CP18-89-000 (confirmed via federalregister.gov, 5 linked documents 2018-2018, including a Notice of Application 2018-03-09 and Notice of Availability of the Environmental Assessment 2018-11-05); the tariff PDF at informationalpostings.natfuel.com/empire/docs/empiretariff.pdf also cites 'CERTIFICATED CAPACITY UNDER DOCKET NO. CP18-89-000' confirming the docket governs this project's capacity.

Not about P2531 directly, but corrects the record for whoever researches P2531/route history: the 2010-vintage Tioga County Extension Project (16 mi, 24-in, Docket CP10-493-000, ~$45.9M estimated cost, +350,000 Dth/d) is a DIFFERENT, earlier (2011 in-service) project than the 2020 Empire North Project -- both involve Tioga County/producer interconnections and it would be easy to conflate them.

summary: P0288 (Empire Pipeline Main Line): existence, classification, operator/owner, length (269 mi), start year (1993) and route (Chippawa ON -> Tioga Co., PA) all confirmed via SEC EDGAR, Oil & Gas Journal, FERC, PHMSA and EIA -- confirmed (caveat). One concern staged: Capacity=300 MMcf/d is mis-sourced (gem.wiki's own footnote is actually about the unrelated 2020 Empire North Expansion project, P2531) and disputed by an independent 1992/93 design-capacity figure of 525 MMcf/d for the original segment -- true current system capacity UNRESOLVED, contested. Diameter (24 in), ConstructionYear (1992) and Operator filled at high tier; FuelSource filled at medium tier (single-origin). Pressure, ProposalYear and SegmentCost left UNRESOLVED (no single system-wide figure exists for this multi-phase aggregate row).
